newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Mobil plans Altona, Adelaide turnarounds in May.
newsitem.headline: Mobil plans Altona, Adelaide turnarounds in May.

text.p: Mobil Australia Ltd plans turnarounds at both its Adelaide and Altona refineries in May, an industry source close to the company said on Thursday.
The source said Mobil would shut down its 75,000-bpd Adelaide refinery while its 27,000-bpd reformer closed for a scheduled catalytic regeneration for the first half of May.
The 55,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) Altona crude distillation unit (CDU) would be shut down for maintenance in late May for two weeks, the source said.
"The whole (Altona) shutdown is for three weeks, but the CDU will be down for around two weeks," the source said.
The source said all three of the company's reformers would be shut down for the three weeks. Mobil's reforming capacity at Altona stands at around 30,000-bpd, industry sources said.
They said the shutdowns would lead to a shortage in gasoline production in Australia and to a rise in imports.
"It should be tighter and there will be be some imports, but not until May when there are a few shutdowns," said one products trader.
Reformers are secondary refining units that produce reformate, a major gasoline blending component.
One industry source said Mobil would not be affected on the crude side by the shutdown.
"There is one crude unit running which will balance the term contracts," the source said, referring to Mobil's other 63,000-bpd CDU at the refinery at Altona, near Melbourne.
Mobil has scheduled the replacement of its existing 24,000-bpd thermal catalytic cracker (TCC) at Altona with a fluid catalytic cracker of the same capacity in the second half of the year.
